newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - May 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - May 27.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Bangladesh has invited Pakistan and India for a three-nation summit in Dhaka in November, Foreign Minister Abdus Samad Azad said on Monday.
Opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) and the Jmaat-e-Islami are unlikely to contest the June 30 parliamentary by-elections to the Manikganj-3 constituency.
Prime MInister Sheikh Hasina is expected to visit Indonesia, Malaysia and the Phillipines in September to bolster economic ties with the ASEAN region.

The proposed Industrial Policy'97 will limit the role of the government to that of a facilitator with the responsibility of creating an enabling environment for attracting increased private investment.
Ministers of four countries will meet in Bangkok on June 6 to sign a declaration floating a new trade bloc, comprising Bangladesh, India, Sri Lanka and Thailand.
Leading economists, during a pre-budget consultation with the Finance Minister S.A.M.S. Kibria on Monday, suggested phasing out of fertiliser subsidy.
The Local Government Commission on Monday submitted its report to the Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina suggesting a four-tier local body structure.
Smith Cogenerations of USA and Bangladesh's Power Development Board (PDB) on Sunday signed an agreement on installation of a 100 megawatt barge mounted power plant near Chittagong. REUTER
